Write a parameter specification

Source: R/ctPar.R
ctPar.Rd

Builds the |-separated cell specification that ctsem's model matrices use, from named arguments.

Usage

ctPar(
  name,
  transform = NA,
  indvarying = NA,
  sdscale = NA,
  tipreds = NULL,
  mean = NA
)

Arguments

name

Parameter name. Two cells given the same name are the same parameter, which is how equality constraints are written.

transform

Transform expression in terms of param, e.g. 'exp(param)'. If omitted, the default for that matrix and cell is used, which differs between, for example, variances, drift diagonals and means.

indvarying

Where the parameter varies: TRUE at every level of the model's id hierarchy, FALSE at none, or the names of the levels it varies at. With id = c('person', 'couple') in ctModel, indvarying = 'couple' gives a parameter that differs between couples but not between the persons within a couple, and TRUE is the same as c('person', 'couple'). With a single id the two forms mean the same thing. The model's pars$indvarying column holds the same values and may be edited directly.

sdscale

Multiplier on the population standard deviation's prior, at every level where the parameter varies. Only meaningful when it varies.

tipreds

Time independent predictors acting on this parameter, as a character vector of names for effects to estimate, e.g. 'age' or c('age', 'sex'). Naming any predictor turns the others off for this cell, so the list is the full set of effects on it. Each name must be one of the model's TIpredNames, or building the model gives an error. character(0) (or tipreds= with nothing after it, in a cell) means no predictor acts on this cell. Leaving the argument out keeps the model's default.

mean

A fixed population mean for a parameter that varies (indvarying), on the scale summary() reports population means on. Only the random effects around it are then estimated, as for a person-level intercept with mean zero. Written into the cell as 'name=value|...', and stored on the model in fixedpopmeans, a named vector that may also be set directly. Needs backend = 'julia'.

Value

A single character string, suitable for a model matrix cell.

Details

The output is the same string the | syntax produces. Fields left at their default are left empty, which the parser reads as unspecified.

The same named fields can also be written directly into a model matrix cell. A cell containing | is read as a |-separated specification. Otherwise a cell with a field of the form name=value is read as a named specification, and anything else as a plain parameter name. These three specify the same parameter:


  MANIFESTMEANS = matrix('mm||TRUE|0.5')
  MANIFESTMEANS = matrix(ctPar('mm', indvarying = TRUE, sdscale = 0.5))
  MANIFESTMEANS = matrix('mm, indvarying=TRUE, sdscale=0.5')

In the named form, fields are separated by commas, the parameter name comes first, and several predictors or levels are given as tipreds=c(age, sex) or indvarying=c(person, couple). Commas inside brackets belong to the value, so transform=pnorm(param, 0, 1) is one field. In the | form, several values are separated by commas, as in 'cross||person,couple'. An unknown field name is an error that names the nearest valid field, so a misspelling such as topreds=age is caught. Comparisons in a state dependent cell (==, >=, <=, !=) and named arguments inside a function call are read as part of the value.

See also

ctModel for the matrices these cells go in.

Examples

ctPar('mm', indvarying = TRUE)
ctPar('drift11', transform = '-exp(param)')
ctPar('mm', indvarying = TRUE, tipreds = c('age', 'sex'))
# varying between couples only, in a model with id = c('person', 'couple')
ctPar('cross', indvarying = 'couple')
# a person-level intercept whose population mean is zero
ctPar('lev', indvarying = TRUE, mean = 0)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# These two models are identical.
model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 1, n.manifest = 1,
  LAMBDA = matrix(1),
  MANIFESTMEANS = matrix(ctPar('mm', indvarying = TRUE, sdscale = 0.5)))

model <- ctModel(type = 'ct', n.latent = 1, n.manifest = 1,
  LAMBDA = matrix(1),
  MANIFESTMEANS = matrix('mm, indvarying=TRUE, sdscale=0.5'))
} # }
